name: Introduction and overview — B-1 Lancer — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — B-1 Lancer
description: Introduction and overview of the B-1 Lancer: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The B-1 Lancer is a four-engine supersonic strategic bomber built by Rockwell (now Boeing), entering service in 1986. Its variable-sweep wings tuck back for high-speed low-level penetration. 104 were built; the fleet later converted to conventional-only weapons and set payload records carrying the largest conventional bomb loads of any U.S. bomber. Baseline facts: Four-engine supersonic bomber; USAF service from 1986; 104 built by Rockwell/Boeing; variable-sweep wings..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: B-1 Lancer: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Four-engine supersonic bomber; USAF service from 1986; 104 built by Rockwell/Boeing; variable-sweep wings.
